quotes.text: MCP server, we work with API behind the scene. This is not a replacement, basically, if I summarize this, because the MCP server is just, okay, it gives the AI the context and behind the scene, the MCP can call APIs

quotes.text: when you need to deal with the agent solution, always do in user permissions, delegated permissions, because in terms of security is to be honest, is better because the user will deal only with data and tools it has access to.

quotes.text: one of the first things to do is, okay, to understand your data because without understanding your data, you are lost.
quotes.speaker: Yves Habersaat

quotes.text: your AI solution needs to be transparent. You need to understand what is performed behind the scene, what data is query, you need to trace, you need to log everything
quotes.speaker: Yves Habersaat
quotes.why: Makes transparency and logging a baseline requirement for trustworthy AI solutions.

chapters.title: Yves' journey and why prompt engineering is not enough
Where Copilot ends and extensibility begins: agents and multi-agent design
Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry and custom development
Data, governance and user versus application permissions
RAG, knowledge sources and the semantic index
Agent lifecycle, AI readiness, trust and rapid-fire round

takeaways: Prompt engineering alone is not enough: organizations still need architects and specialists who understand the customer, the data and the underlying technologies.
Yves recommends a multi-agent approach with clearly scoped agents, Copilot Studio for low-code needs and custom development when the orchestration or models must be customized.
MCP servers sit in front of existing APIs, while delegated user permissions, clean and classified data, and transparent logging keep enterprise agents secure and trustworthy.
hook: Once organizations use Copilot seriously, the question shifts from writing better prompts to connecting Copilot with business data, APIs and processes. In this conversation, Microsoft MVP Yves Habersaat explains Copilot extensibility, agent architecture, MCP, RAG and permissions for architects, developers and IT decision-makers. Learn when to use Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry or custom code and how to build production-grade agents securely.
